steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxation to influence the economy. Expansionary: increase spending/cut taxes to boost demand. Contractionary: cut spending/raise taxes to reduce demand.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Expansionary fiscal policy can achieve growth and reduce unemployment but may cause inflation and increase the budget deficit.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A budget deficit (spending > revenue) increases national debt; a surplus (revenue > spending) reduces it. The UK has run deficits for most of the last 50 years.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Fiscal policy can redistribute income (progressive taxes, welfare spending) and correct market failures (public goods, taxing externalities).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how expansionary fiscal policy could help an economy in recession. | Describe what is meant by a budget deficit and one consequence of a persistent deficit. | Evaluate whether fiscal policy is an effective tool for managing the economy.
